speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ulcerative Colitis

The combination of mucus, urgency, incomplete evacuation, and relief of pain after defecation strongly suggests inflammatory bowel disease. However, your history of camping with a sick contact makes infectious colitis a possibility. Given the duration of four months, infection is less likely, but we must confirm. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture_and_OVA_and_PCA.
